newsitem.title: GHANA: U.S. planes airlift peacekeepers to Liberia.
newsitem.headline: U.S. planes airlift peacekeepers to Liberia.

text.p: U.S. planes began airlifting additional West African peacekeepers to Liberia on Tuesday, ahead of national elections in the shattered West African nation on May 30, military officials said.
The first of 500 extra Ghanaian peacekeepers left their capital Accra on board a U.S. transport plane, witnesses said.

U.S. C-130 transport planes, based in Ivory Coast's commercial capital Abidjan for the duration of the exercise, will ferry in over 1,000 extra soldiers for the 10,000-strong, Nigerian-led ECOMOG peacekeeping force.
The 500 from Ghana will boost the Ghanaian contingent to 1,336 men.
The planes will also ferry in 600 soldiers from Mali, 320 soldiers from Burkina Faso and a 90-strong medical team from Ivory Coast.
Under a peace deal brokered by its neighbours, Liberia will hold presidential and parliamentary elections on May 30 to end seven years of civil war.
ECOMOG commander General Victor Malu says he is satisfied with the level of disarmament of the faction fighters after that part of the countdown to peace ended earlier this month.
Founded by freed American slaves in 1847, Liberia has strong emotional ties with the United States.
A U.S. naval task force airlifted U.S. and other foreign nationals out of the capital Monrovia last April and May during a flare-up of the war in the capital.
